title: Red blood cell diagram sheet
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: The periodic table (8F); breathing and respiration (8C)
source: Seeded from science/y8 lesson 37 (Red blood cell diagram sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 37: Getting oxygen to cells: blood and haemoglobin. To understand how red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to respiring cells

picture.alt: Red blood cells under a microscope
picture.draw: Draw and label: Red blood cell diagram sheet

questions.q: Explain why carbon monoxide is dangerous.
questions.a: It joins haemoglobin instead of oxygen, so less oxygen reaches cells for respiration
questions.model: What carries oxygen? Haemoglobin. What does CO do? Takes its place. So less oxygen gets to cells, and respiration slows.

questions.q: Name the part of blood that carries glucose.
Give one adaptation of red blood cells.
questions.a: No nucleus, biconcave shape, or small and flexible

questions.q: Draw a red blood cell (top and side view) and label three adaptations with their benefit.
questions.a: Biconcave disc (surface area), no nucleus (more haemoglobin), small and flexible (fits capillaries)
questions.model: Teacher draws the side view on screen: a disc thinner in the middle.

questions.q: Why do people who live at high altitude often have more red blood cells?
questions.a: To carry enough oxygen when each breath has less oxygen.

questions.q: Explain why a CO alarm is needed near a gas boiler.
questions.a: Faulty burning makes CO, which has no smell or colour; an alarm detects it before people are harmed.

questions.q: Big question: why do climbers tire quickly high up?
questions.a: Less oxygen per breath reaches their cells for respiration.
